frameTiming.harness: headless Chromium via SwiftShader (software rasteriser, no GPU)
frameTiming.caveat: Absolute frame rates from this harness are a floor, not a prediction for real hardware. Useful for regression detection, not for asserting the 60 FPS budget.

measured.persistenceAcrossReload: 1 segment / 45 fixes survived a full page reload (verified in a browser)
measured.androidBuild: BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 2m 4s, 86 tasks; app-debug.apk 6.3 MB; installed and launched on device

map.notes: Three synchronised planes (imagery / survey / labels). Verified at five zoom levels from planet to street.

fog-of-war.notes: Two-pass WebGL mask: MAX-blended coverage buffer, destination-out composite. Minimum on-screen radius keeps corridors legible when zoomed out. Live fixes now reveal territory incrementally as they arrive.

demo-data.notes: Deterministic 18-month history in the subject's local time. Road-following waypoints; regression tests for impossible journeys, unbacked visit counts and out-of-range timestamps.

exploration.notes: H3 res-9 cells for statistics, continuous stamps for rendering. Accuracy drives reveal radius and strength; flights reveal endpoints only.

routes.notes: 1151 segments collapse to 43 unique routes; travel frequency drives line weight.

statistics.notes: Pure aggregation, 23 tests, ~3ms on the full dataset. Chart excludes flights so one long-haul does not flatten 18 months of daily life.

achievements.notes: 13 achievements; the demo user earns 10. Country attribution inferred from city proximity, with the limitation stated in the UI.

search.notes: 496 indexed entries over user history plus a curated world gazetteer. 0.072ms per query. Results carry exploration state.

gps.notes: Real geolocation with battery profiles. Every documented fault surfaces distinctly; bad fixes are marked excluded, never deleted. A walk reveals ground in real time and announces genuinely new cells; screen wake lock holds the display on mid-walk. A provider abstraction selects an Android foreground-service source inside the native shell; the browser source is foreground-only and the UI states that.

permissions.notes: Insecure context reported separately from denial; mid-session revocation detected.

timeline.notes: 453 days grouped and virtualised. Replay interpolates on real elapsed time, so a stop in a journey visibly pauses.

storage.notes: IndexedDB persistence: fixes written as they arrive, walks committed as segments, interrupted walks recovered on next launch. Lossless export retained. 14 tests.

ui.notes: One design system across map HUD, four drawers, search and onboarding. Phone layout reorganises to bottom sheets with thumb-reachable tracking control.

onboarding.notes: One screen, two honest choices; demo needs no location permission.

privacy.notes: Top-level panel. Home masking and delete-all do real work; deletion returns the map to unexplored.

performance.notes: Frame intervals and heap are now measured (pnpm perf). Memory stability is verified: zero heap growth across two identical interaction passes. The 60 FPS budget remains UNVERIFIED because this environment has no GPU. Route rendering recedes at street zoom, which removed the dominant source of visual noise.

places.notes: Places exist in the model and statistics; there is no dedicated places surface or favouriting UI.

pwa.notes: Installable: manifest, maskable icons, minimal network-first service worker. Map tiles are deliberately not cached — a walk would exhaust the storage quota. Cannot do background location: service workers have no geolocation API (verified empirically).

location-history.notes: Turns recorded fixes into segments with inferred mode. Rejects stationary jitter via a bounding-box span guard, not just cumulative path length.

android.notes: Debug APK builds (AGP 9.4 / Gradle 9.6), installs and launches on a Galaxy Z Fold (SM_F976U1). Foreground service merged with foregroundServiceType="location"; permissions come from the plugin, no manual manifest edits. Background tracking itself is not yet confirmed on a real walk.

openIssues.summary: The 60 FPS budget is still unverified: the headless harness renders via SwiftShader with no GPU, so it can only detect regressions, not confirm the budget. Needs a run on real hardware.
Subsequence matching is loose — 'tok' matches 'Thessaloniki'. Exact prefixes still rank first.
Revealed imagery reads dark where a narrow corridor crosses dense tree canopy at city zoom.

Demo routes interpolate straight lines between hand-placed waypoints, so they do not follow street geometry exactly. Route lines now recede at street zoom where the reveal corridor is the accurate record.
Android APK builds, installs and launches, but background tracking has not been exercised on a real walk: the screen-off, phone-in-pocket behaviour is still unconfirmed.
Recorded walks are not grouped into trips, so each walk is its own journey in the timeline.

resolvedIssues: MapLibre stylesheet load order collapsed map containers to zero height.
Fog mask rendered nothing: modelViewProjectionMatrix expects world-pixel coords, not normalised mercator.
Matrix uploads silently rejected because MapLibre supplies Float64Array where uniformMatrix4fv requires Float32Array.
Stencil/scissor state inherited from MapLibre discarded the composite pass.
Radius folded into the corner attribute collapsed the radial falloff.
Duplicate place labels across the fog boundary; fixed with a dedicated label plane.
Demo road trips interpolated straight lines across San Francisco Bay.
380 stacked commute polylines compounded alpha into opaque bands over the map.
MapLibre rejects a zoom expression nested inside a multiply.
Rail stretched to the drawer's width and hid its own buttons behind it.
Demo routine generated in UTC put a San Francisco commute at 03:45 local.
Local-time generation dated the tail of the history after its declared end.
Place.visitCount was inflated relative to the visit records backing it.
Performance was entirely unmeasured; frame timing and heap instrumentation now exist and show no per-frame retention.
Live tracking drew a position marker but never revealed territory — new fixes did not reach the fog mask.
Survey ink was too pale to read; road hierarchy and water were indistinguishable at a glance.
Local errands and weekend routes cut straight diagonals through city blocks.
Route lines dominated street zoom as a starburst of overlapping strokes.
Vite flipped to HTTPS merely because .certs/ existed, silently breaking the verification harness.
Live-tracked walks were lost on reload; history is now persisted in IndexedDB.
A suspended page bridged its tracking gap with a straight line; the trail now breaks and reports missed time.
Deleting history was session-only; deletion now wipes storage and persists the dismissal.
IndexedDB transaction was awaited mid-flight, which can auto-commit before follow-up writes land.
Android build failed on getDefaultProguardFile("proguard-android.txt"), which AGP 9 rejects; fixed in the app and, via a committed pnpm patch, in the background-geolocation plugin.
Gradle read the unpatched plugin path until cap sync regenerated capacitor.settings.gradle.
